filename: Two sources of uncertainty in estimating tephra volumes from isopachs_ perspectives and quantification.pdf
title: Two sources of uncertainty in estimating tephra volumes from isopachs: perspectives and quantification
testbed_rationale: This paper focuses on analytical and empirical curve fitting (exponential, power-law, Weibull) and statistical uncertainty quantification for volcanological tephra deposits, not machine learning parameterizations or emulators.
pain_points: Model uncertainty due to empirical/analytical curves deviating from true deposit thinning patterns
Fitting in log-transformed space (log thickness vs square root isopach area) hides large relative errors in real space and area-integrated volume
Uncertainty in extrapolation (proximal and distal volumes beyond observed isopachs) cannot be validated against data
extraction_notes: The paper acknowledges partial support from the NSF STC LEAP (Award 2019625). It uses statistical/empirical curve-fitting methods rather than ML.
